clusters.text: The iPhone Duo goes on sale this Friday, October 23, but if you were hoping to just walk into an Apple Store and pick one up, you may want to rethink that plan. In a statement, Apple says there will be "limited" availability for walk-in customers, and given the "extraordinary" demand since pre-orders began last week, it expects that supply to sell out quickly. Limited walk-in stock will be available in the US, Australia, Austria, Belgium, Canada, Mexico, Germany, the Netherlands, Singapore, Spain, Sweden, Switzerland, Türkiye, and the UK. Certain Apple Stores in Italy will have some too, though Apple didn't say which ones. In Macao, walk-in sales will only happen on launch day, and inventory will be limited there as well. Things are stricter in France, China, Hong Kong, India, Japan, Malaysia, South Korea, Taiwan, Thailand, and the UAE, where you won't be able to buy the Duo as a walk-in customer on launch day at all. Instead, you'll need to reserve a pickup time slot through Apple's online store. That's easier said than done for now - the store currently tells people to check back on Saturday, October 24, so it's unclear if reservations will even be possible on launch day itself. Apple restricts walk-in sales in some countries partly to manage crowd sizes and partly to fight scalpers, which is also why it has capped iPhone Duo purchases at two per person . If you've already pre-ordered, there's some good news, as shipping dates have been pulled forward for many people after slipping all the way to January . clusters.text: ORBITERS, LANDERS and rovers have travelled to Mars, but none has returned. The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) intends for that to change. On October 20th its Martian Moons eXploration (MMX) mission lifted off from Tanegashima, an island in southern Japan. The probe will spend the next year travelling to Mars, where it aims to land on Phobos, the larger of the planet’s two moons, collect at least ten grams of rock and dust, and return the haul to Earth in 2031. Planetary scientists hope the mission will resolve a long-standing puzzle: how Mars’s moons were formed—and, in the process, reveal much about the planet itself.Phobos and Mars’s other moon, Deimos, are small, respectively about 22km and 12km across, and look like lumpy potatoes. That might suggest they are asteroids that were captured by Mars’s gravitational field after straying too close. Captured asteroids, however, usually have tilted, elliptical orbits, whereas both moons follow nearly circular paths around the planet’s equator. That hints at another possible origin: a giant collision that threw debris into orbit that later gathered into moons.JAXA has spent over a decade developing MMX, working with the space agencies of America, Europe and Australia. The mission builds on Japan’s record of returning samples from space. Its Hayabusa mission collected small amounts of grains from Itokawa, an asteroid which comes close to Earth, and brought them home in 2010. Its successor, Hayabusa2, brought back five grams of material—well above the mission’s target—from Ryugu, another near-Earth asteroid, in 2020. The samples proved rich in water-bearing molecules and organic compounds, offering clues to how asteroids may have carried the ingredients for life to Earth.MMX’s mission is more demanding. Phobos’s surface gravity is roughly one-2,000th of Earth’s, but it is 40 times greater than Ryugu’s. That is strong enough to pose a crash risk for a delicate spacecraft, explains Erik Asphaug, a planetary scientist at the University of Arizona. The Hayabusa missions also followed a “touch-and-go” method in which the spacecraft briefly kissed the asteroids. In contrast, MMX will land on Phobos and extract samples from beneath its surface.And MMX’s makers want to do a lot more during its three years orbiting Mars. clusters.text: Meta, the company behind Facebook, Instagram and WhatsApp has been hit with its largest fine ever for its business practices. A judge in New Mexico on Wednesday ordered the company to pay $25bn (£18.6bn) following a two-week trial earlier this year that found it had spent years lying to the public about how it handled Facebook user data. "The lies extend beyond Facebook's data practices as well," the judge said, adding they went to "the heart of Facebook's core business practices". Meta's head lawyer CJ Mahoney said the ruling made it "all but impossible to do business in the state of New Mexico". The company intends to appeal, a move Mahoney said will be successful. The fine is the largest to date against Meta, which has either been fined or agreed to settle several other lawsuits this year, including an $18bn deal with California over child safety. New Mexico's lawsuit stemmed from the role of Meta, then still doing business as Facebook, in what became known as the Cambridge Analytica scandal. That firm utilised data and information from millions of Facebook users as part of its work in political consulting, including on work related to the 2016 US Presidential election, which saw Donald Trump elected for the first time. New Mexico had also accused Meta of intentionally misleading the public on how it benefitted from content that included hate speech, and how such rules against it were enforced. The jury found the company had intentionally misled the public on those claims, too. Meta disputed those accusations. "At its core, this lawsuit seeks to impose a tax on speech to enforce new rules for what people can say online," Mahoney added. Lawyers for New Mexico sued the company over many statements Meta executives had made over the years that user data was never shared with or accessed by third parties without a user's permission, when in reality it had been. They claimed that the entire population of the state, roughly two million people, was impacted by Meta's dishonesty regarding the way it controlled user data. A jury found that Meta had violated state laws more than 40 million times. clusters.text: For a little over 20 minutes, Aston Villa could look down on the rest of Europe. They had scaled the Champions League summit on goal difference when Henrik Heggheim put through his own net and the fact was not lost on the Holte End, who reflected their position in song and perhaps allowed themselves another glimpse back to the days when their supremacy was undisputed. “We’ve conquered before, we’re prepared for more,” the pre-match tifo display had read. clusters.text: Kvaratskhelia out for months with a torn ACL in his right knee, while Dembele and Marquinhos suffer thigh muscle tears. Paris Saint-Germain have been handed a triple injury setback after their stunning Champions League win over Barcelona, with star players Khvicha Kvaratskhelia, Ousmane Dembele and Marquinhos forced out of action in the coming weeks. Kvaratskhelia sustained an anterior cruciate ligament (ACL) tear in his right knee, making him unavailable for months, while forward Dembele and captain Marquinhos sustained thigh muscle injuries during the match on Tuesday. “Having suffered a torn anterior cruciate ligament in his right knee during yesterday’s match against FC Barcelona, Khvicha Kvaratskhelia is set to undergo surgery in the coming days,” PSG said in a statement. Kvaratskhelia landed awkwardly after sprinting back to make a tackle on Xavi Espart early in the second half and looked in severe pain as he clutched his knee. Last year’s Ballon d’Or winner Dembele (left thigh) and Marquinhos (right thigh) are both set to miss several weeks. Dembele pulled up clutching the back of his left thigh following a run down the left in the 19th minute of the game. Kvaratskhelia and 32-year-old Marquinhos were replaced on the hour mark at the Parc des Princes, where two-time defending champions PSG won 4-2 for a third straight win in the competition. PSG coach Luis Enrique used Dembele sparingly in the French league last season and has already rested him twice in Ligue 1 this campaign. The France star, who scored six goals at the World Cup, struggled with injuries last season and had been beset by leg muscle injuries at his previous club Barcelona. The 2024-25 campaign, which led to him winning the men’s Ballon d’Or, saw Dembele playing 50 games overall in a season for the first time in his career. PSG host Lyon in Ligue 1 on Sunday, with both sides level on points at the top of the standings.

clusters.text: Pirelli have confirmed the tyre compounds that will be in use for the United States Grand Prix weekend in Austin. Next up on the 2026 F1 calendar is the United States Grand Prix, held at Austin's Circuit of The Americas – and tyre suppliers Pirelli have confirmed the compounds that will be in use throughout the weekend. For this year's event, the C2 has been selected as the hard compound, with the C3 as the medium and C4 as the soft. This marks a change from last season, when Pirelli brought three non-consecutive compounds (the C1, C3 and C4) for what was a Sprint weekend. The usual Grand Prix format is in place this time around, so drivers will get two sets of the hard tyre (marked white), three sets of the medium tyre (marked yellow), and eight sets of the soft tyre (marked red), as well as access to the green intermediate tyre and the blue full wets, should they be required. An extra set of softs is reserved for those who reach Q3 in Qualifying, while all drivers must use at least two different slick compounds during the race, providing the track is dry. "The Austin circuit, which is 5.513km long, features a mix of high-speed corners, rapid direction changes and slower sections that demand strong traction," reads Pirelli's weekend preview. "To be competitive, teams must combine good straight-line speed with efficient aerodynamic load through the more technical sections, an aspect that becomes even more important with the current generation of Formula 1 cars. "From a tyre perspective, COTA places demands on both axles. In the first sector, characterised by fast corners and direction changes inspired by some of Europe’s great circuits, the front tyres will be placed under particular stress. In the third sector, meanwhile, the numerous acceleration zones out of slow corners will tend to generate thermal degradation primarily on the rear tyres. "The asphalt surface is not particularly abrasive. A section of the circuit between Turns 9 and 11 was resurfaced earlier this year. However, the ageing effect on the remainder of the track continues to be significant and contributes to high wear levels. clusters.snippet: Katie Boulter moves into the quarter-finals of the Japan Open after she beat Viktorija Golubic in less than an hour.
clusters.text: Katie Boulter is British number two after Sonny Kartal replaced her at the top of the rankings on Monday Katie Boulter moved into the quarter-finals of the Japan Open after she beat Viktorija Golubic in less than an hour. The British number two defeated her Swiss opponent 6-2 6-1 in Osaka and will face either Croatia's Antonia Ruzic or American Kayla Day in the next round. Boulter saved a break point in the opening game but dominated from 2-2 in the first set, winning nine games in a row before Golubic took the penultimate game of the match. The 30-year-old lost the British number one spot to Sonny Kartal on Monday, but is set to retake the position following her run this week. Boulter, who is seeded eighth in the competition, said she was pleased with how she handled "difficult conditions", with a strong wind affecting play. "I think one of the biggest things for me is staying patient in the wind," she said. "Sometimes I can get a little frustrated, and I'm very pleased that I didn't allow that to affect me today and I think I ended up playing some really good tennis in the second set. I'm really pleased with the performance." Later on Wednesday, Britain's Jacob Fearnley missed out on a place in the quarter-finals of the European Open as he fell to a 7-6 (7-4) 6-2 defeat by Frenchman Clement Chidekh in Brussels.

clusters.title: Rare Red Sand Boa rescued in Ranchi; Haryana man detained
clusters.text: A rare red sand boa snake was rescued in Ranchi’s Lalpur area after police recovered it from a bag carried by a man from Haryana. The Lalpur police informed the Forest Department, which has launched an investigation into the case.Police had stopped three people on suspicion of suspicious activities. Two of them fled when they saw the police, while the third was detained. During a search, officers recovered the snake from his bag and alerted the Forest Department. A forest team subsequently rescued the snake safely.The detained man, identified as Tilu, is a resident of Sonipat in Haryana. During questioning, he reportedly told forest officials that the snake belonged to his friend. Police and forest officials are investigating where the snake was sourced, why it was brought to Ranchi and what role the two absconding men played.Ranchi Divisional Forest Officer Shrikant said the red sand boa is a rare species. The snake is often associated with claims of fetching extremely high prices in international markets, but reports of its alleged worth running into crores of rupees are not supported by any verified or standard market valuation.The species has reportedly been targeted by illegal wildlife traders due to superstitions and traditional beliefs. In some countries, including China and parts of Southeast Asia, folklore and beliefs associated with traditional medicine have been cited as factors driving demand. Some people also associate the snake with wealth and good fortune.Authorities are investigating the circumstances surrounding the recovery and the possibility of illegal wildlife trade.

clusters.title: Land case backlog puts Prayagraj revenue officials in the dock | Hindustan Times
clusters.text: The divisional commissioner has ordered disciplinary action against tehsildars and naib tehsildars in Prayagraj and Pratapgarh after finding that over 1,500 land dispute cases in the former and 712 in the latter have exceeded the mandatory six-month disposal deadline.Official records indicate a widespread delay across the region. In addition to the backlog in Prayagraj and Pratapgarh, 271 cases remain pending beyond the deadline in Kaushambi, while Fatehpur reports 245 such cases.Divisional commissioner Lokesh M issued these directives on Monday following a performance review of revenue officials, which he deemed “unsatisfactory.” Despite previous instructions to expedite case resolutions, officials responsible for the files have failed to clear the backlog.The review also highlighted shortcomings in grievance redressal. While officials were asked to ensure an 80% satisfaction rate for complaints filed through the Integrated Grievance Redressal System (IGRS) and a 90% complainant-contact rate, the targets remain unmet. Satisfaction levels currently stand at 63.92% in Prayagraj, 59.03% in Kaushambi, 55.25% in Fatehpur and 59.19% in Pratapgarh. The rate of contacting complainants is 79.98% in Prayagraj, 79.08% in Kaushambi, 75.02% in Fatehpur and 75.98% in Pratapgarh.The commissioner also flagged delays in uncontested succession cases, which must be resolved within seven days. The number of pending uncontested succession cases is 230 in Prayagraj and 271 in Pratapgarh. Mutation cases, which must be decided within 90 days, have also piled up, with 707 pending in Prayagraj, 618 in Pratapgarh, 182 in Kaushambi and 185 in Fatehpur beyond the prescribed period.Inspections in Kunda and Chail tehsils also revealed that record-keeping protocols for encroachment cases and grievance registers were not being followed. Consequently, the divisional commissioner has directed the district magistrates of all four affected districts to initiate formal disciplinary proceedings against the concerned ADMs, SDMs, tehsildars, naib tehsildars and other relevant revenue personnel.
